It was cleaner than its caption claimed -- but by luck, and luck is not a property you get to keep silently. SECOND ADDITION -- EXCURSION CONTINUATION (hazard) curve. Every existing view of the MFE column is MARGINAL ('26% reached 2.0R'), which says how many trades ended in the tail but not WHERE the population thins. Read conditionally the shape is not smooth, it is a cliff: 0->0.5R 84%, 0.5->1.0R 38%, 1.0->1.5R 83%, 1.5->2.0R 100%. ALL the attrition sits in ONE band. This entry produces two populations -- ~62% of trades that get off the ground are dead cats that bounce 0.5-0.8R and die, and the rest clear 1.0R and then run to 2.0R+ near-deterministically. THE DISCRIMINATING LEVEL IS +1.0R, NOT +2.5R. This SUPPORTS the locked TRAIL_START_R=2.50 rather than attacking it: 2.50 sits above the cliff, so the ratchet never arms on a dead cat, and it is the conservative end of a wide safe plateau [1.0R, 2.5R]. CENSORING is printed as a first-class field, not a footnote: the ratchet arms at TRAIL_START_R and closes the trade THERE, so no poll can observe an MFE materially above it on a trade that armed. Below 2.50R the column measures the market; at and above it, it measures our own exit. 'Only 11% reached 2.5R' is not a fact about the entry -- it is the level at which we stop watching.
